title: Mesh-based Nelder–Mead algorithm for inequality constrained optimization: C. Audet, C. Tribes
contribution: Extends Nelder–Mead to inequality-constrained optimization by embedding it as a Mads search step, so it inherits Mads convergence; reports improved solution quality (abstract).
problem_entry: NM is widely used despite lacking convergence support and is limited to unconstrained problems (abstract).
key_idea: NM as a Mads Search step: heuristic power, Mads guarantees (abstract).
assumptions: Inequality-constrained problems (abstract); constraint treatment (EB/PB) not stated in the abstract.
experiments: Numerical experiments showing improved solution quality with the NM search step (abstract); problem set, competitors and budget not read.
positioning: Positions against NM's missing convergence support while acknowledging its wide use (abstract).

method_links.note: A guarantee-free heuristic (NM) is admitted only as a Search step and the method inherits all of the Mads analysis.
Direct abstract support for the "wrap heuristics" pattern already cited in SKILL.md.

transferable: To publish a popular heuristic that has no convergence theory, reimplement it as the Search step of a convergent direct search (trial points on the mesh), let the Poll carry the proof, and report the improvement attributable to that search step (abstract).

quotes.text: This is done through a search step of the mesh adaptive direct search (Mads) algorithm, inspired by the NM algorithm.
The proposed algorithm does not suffer from the NM lack of convergence, but instead inherits from the totality of the Mads convergence analysis.

title: Robust optimization of noisy blackbox problems using the mesh adaptive direct search algorithm
contribution: Robust-MADS: a MADS variant for noisy unconstrained blackboxes that smooths the objective with past evaluations instead of resampling (abstract).
problem_entry: Noise creates artificial solutions where MADS can stall (abstract).
key_idea: Smoothing from the evaluation history, no resampling (abstract).
experiments: Noisy problems from the literature (abstract); protocol not read.
positioning: Implicitly contrasts with resampling-based noise handling ("rather than resampling points", abstract).
limits_future: not read (the unconstrained restriction is stated, abstract)

method_links.note: Step 5 recommends robust MADS for noisy blackboxes; the abstract confirms its mechanism: smoothing from past evaluations, unconstrained case only.

method_links.method: new-pattern candidate: evaluation-economical noise handling (reuse cached evaluations instead of resampling)
method_links.note: Smoothing uses previously evaluated points rather than new samples.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: evaluation-economical noise handling: reuse cached evaluations instead of resampling
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Robust-MADS smooths the objective "using previously evaluated function evaluations, rather than resampling points".

transferable: Before spending evaluations on replications to fight noise, smooth the objective with values already in the evaluation cache; resampling becomes the fallback, not the default (abstract).
coauthors: A. Ihaddadene, S. Le Digabel, C. Tribes

quotes.text: Blackbox optimization problems are often contaminated with numerical noise, and direct search methods such as the Mesh Adaptive Direct Search (MADS) algorithm may get stuck at solutions artificially created by the noise.
We propose a way to smooth out the objective function of an unconstrained problem using previously evaluated function evaluations, rather than resampling points.

title: Efficient solution of quadratically constrained quadratic subproblems within the mesh adaptive direct search algorithm
contribution: Three structure-exploiting QCQP solvers (l1 penalty, augmented Lagrangian, and a new combination) for the quadratic-model search step of MADS, implemented in NOMAD and tested on 65 analytic problems and 4 engineering simulations (abstract).
problem_entry: Quadratic-model search in MADS produces QCQP subproblems that need an efficient solver (abstract).
key_idea: Exploit the quadratic structure of the models; combine exact penalty and augmented Lagrangian (abstract).
assumptions: Constrained blackbox problems; quadratic models of objective and constraints inside the search step (abstract).
experiments: 65 analytical test problems and 4 simulation-based engineering applications, inside NOMAD (abstract); profiles and baselines not read.
positioning: Trajectory note (inferred from title): QCQP, the subject of the 1997 thesis Ch. 5 (card b2-01), returns here as a subproblem inside DFO; the abstract does not make this link.

method_links.note: The quadratic models live in an optional, "versatile search step"; the paper improves that Search, not the Poll.
The methods are implemented within NOMAD.
Two problem layers (65 analytic + 4 simulation-based engineering applications); competitors and profile type not read.

transferable: When a Search step generates a stream of structured subproblems, make the subproblem solver the research object: build several solvers that exploit the structure, implement them in the host code, and compare them on both an analytic set and real simulations (abstract).
coauthors: N. Amaioua, A.R. Conn, S. Le Digabel

quotes.text: One of the optional MADS features is a versatile search step in which quadratic models are built leading to a series of quadratically constrained quadratic subproblems.

These methods are implemented within the NOMAD software package and their impact are assessed through computational experiments on 65 analytical test problems and 4 simulation-based engineering applications.

title: The mesh adaptive direct search algorithm for granular and discrete variables
contribution: A Mads variant whose mesh update progressively increases precision so it handles granular variables, and discrete variables as a corollary, tested in NOMAD (abstract).
problem_entry: Mads is built for continuous variables; many practical variables have a controlled number of decimals (abstract).
key_idea: Redesign the mesh-refinement rule around variable granularity (abstract).
assumptions: Granular variables with a controlled number of decimals (abstract).
experiments: Computational results with NOMAD (abstract); protocol not read.
positioning: Builds on Mads's continuous-variable design and Clarke-based analysis (abstract).

method_links.note: The new pathology is handled by changing the mesh update, the structure the Poll relies on, not by adding a Search step.
Algorithm design for a new blackbox pathology (granular/discrete variables) inside MADS.
Computational results are presented with NOMAD.

quotes.text: This modification involves a new way of updating the underlying mesh so that the precision is progressively increased.
A corollary of this new approach is the ability to treat discrete variables.

title: Constrained blackbox optimization with the NOMAD solver on the COCO constrained test suite
contribution: NOMAD (MADS with progressive barrier) vs CMA-ES on COCO's bbob-constrained suite, reported with COCO graphs and constrained data profiles; concludes that these tools are complementary and many graphs are needed (abstract).
problem_entry: New COCO bbob-constrained suite; constrained blackbox optimization (abstract).
key_idea: Evaluate one solver with two communities' benchmarking tools and compare the tools themselves (abstract).
assumptions: Quantifiable and relaxable constraints handled by the progressive barrier (abstract).
experiments: NOMAD (MADS + PB) vs CMA-ES on the COCO bbob-constrained suite; COCO postprocessing graphs plus data profiles adapted to constraints (abstract).
positioning: Brings a DFO tool (data profiles) into an evolutionary-computation platform and venue (abstract).
writing: Abstract ends on a methodological warning rather than a performance claim (abstract).
limits_future: Warns that benchmarking tools and their variations can disagree (abstract).

method_links.note: Cross-community benchmarking on the evolutionary-computation home ground (GECCO, COCO, CMA-ES), with data profiles adapted to constraints and a call to use complementary tools together.
The progressive barrier is used for quantifiable and relaxable constraints.
MADS enters the comparison through its NOMAD implementation.

transferable: When you benchmark on another community's platform, report both the platform's native postprocessing and your own community's profiles (adapted to constraints if needed), and say where they disagree (abstract).
coauthors: S. Le Digabel, L. Salomon, C. Tribes

quotes.text: Computational tests are illustrated with the postprocessing graphs from the COCO platform, as well as with data profiles, an established tool in the derivative-free optimization community, adapted here for the constrained case.
The results illustrate that researchers must be very careful with the use of these tools, which are complementary and should ideally be used together.
